I farm the way I always have: I look at what worked last year, I look at what the better fields around me did, and I do not gamble too much. I have 12 mu total, and with wheat-maize rotation being my main way, I will keep most land in wheat then summer maize, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. Wheat and maize feed the house and bring steady money, so I will put 8 mu into wheat-maize and 4 mu into cotton. I have a well, so I will use water when the crop is really asking for it, not just wait for the sky. Fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will not underfeed. On wheat land, I will put a solid base dressing and then add more urea at jointing. For maize, I will feed it a bit heavier because if maize is thin, the ears come small and there is no fixing it later. Cotton I will not push as hard as maize, but I will still give enough so the plants hold bolls. I mostly follow what I saw work nearby: improved wheat seed, hybrid maize seed, and improved cotton seed if I can get decent seed at a fair price. I will plough for wheat, usually do rotary work for maize after wheat harvest because time is tight, and rotary for cotton too because it saves labor. If insects or disease show up, I will spray; if the field stays clean, I will not waste extra medicine. That is how I will run it this year.
